title: Man. Post. Cap. II §III: Placeus — third acceptio not the question; alienissimus; before §XIV
pass_a_gloss: Third finally; He would pretend that that third acceptation of Christ's justice for justice inhering in us is that which is understood when it is asked whether Christ's justice is imputed to us, or not? Which is false. For in that question Christ's justice is opposed to our justice implanted in us. But I, against those acceptations of Adamic sin concerning which I said there is consensus that it is imputed, removed them from the status of the question to be agitated among us, and indeed in most clear words. Wherefore I was most alien from every ludification.
pass_b_english: Third and last: he would pretend that that third sense of Christ's righteousness—as righteousness inhering in us—is what is meant when we ask whether Christ's righteousness is imputed to us or not. That is false. In that question Christ's righteousness is set over against our righteousness implanted in us. I, on the contrary, removed from the state of the question we are debating among ourselves those senses of Adamic sin concerning which I said there is consensus that it is imputed—and I did so in the clearest words. So I stand wholly alien to every mockery.
source_text: Tertio denique; Ille prae se ferret tertiam illam justitiae Christi acceptionem pro justitia nobis inhaerente, esse eam, quae intelligitur, cum quaeritur, utrum justitia Christi nobis imputetur, necne? Id quod falsum est. Opponitur enim justitia Christi in ea quaestione nostrae justitiae nobis insitae. Ego vero contra istas acceptiones peccati Adamici, quibus illud imputari dixi consensum esse, removi a statu quaestionis inter nos agitandae, et quidem disertissimis verbis. Quare ab omni ludificatione alienissimus fui.

choices.choice: Third acceptio not the justification question; removed from status; stop before §XIV
